The overall average is the mean of `bandusagepct` over all telescopes with non-null values, so each telescope counts once. Keep stations whose average is strictly above the overall average.
Same as 1, but keep stations whose average is greater than or equal to the overall average.
Same as 1, but the overall average is taken over telescopes that have a non-null `bandusagepct` and also belong to a station present in `observatories`. A join to `observatories` would enforce this.
Same as 1, but only stations with at least one non-null `bandusagepct` reading are considered. Stations whose telescopes all have NULL values are excluded, since their average is undefined.
Same as 1, but the overall average is the mean of the per-station averages, so each station counts equally. The question says telescopes are weighted, so this reading is less likely.

Same as 1, but "telescopes" are restricted to those that have recorded signals in `signals`. The overall average would then cover only those telescopes, and a join through `telescref` would enforce it.

Same as 1, but the output includes the station's average and the difference (station average minus overall average). The difference is computed as unrounded floating-point values, and results are sorted by the difference descending with a limit of 10.
Same as 1, but ties in the difference at the top-10 cutoff are broken arbitrarily, or by station name ascending.
Same as 1, but the output is the top 10 stations by difference with only the station name, the average and the difference columns, and no telescope counts.
Same as 1, but the station is identified by `telescopes.observstation` alone, with no join to `observatories`. Stations that exist only in `observatories` with no telescopes are excluded.
Same as 1, but the station is taken from `observatories.observstation` through a join. Stations with no telescopes are excluded because their average is undefined.

Same as 1, but "missing values" also covers empty strings or sentinel values such as 0 or negative numbers in `bandusagepct`, in addition to NULLs. These are excluded from both the station averages and the overall average.
Same as 1, but "without rounding" applies only to the displayed values. Comparisons and sorting use the full-precision floating-point values.

Same as 1, but the overall average is computed over all telescopes in `telescopes`, including those whose `observstation` has no matching row in `observatories`. A telescope with a NULL or orphaned station would still count toward the overall average, but it would not be shown as a station.

Same as 1, but the comparison "above the overall average" is applied to the difference, so the difference must be strictly positive. Floating-point error could make this differ from comparing the averages directly.

Same as 1, but station identifiers are matched after trimming whitespace and normalizing case. This addresses `observstation` being CHAR(60) in the documentation, which implies space padding, so stations with differing padding or casing would be merged into one group.
Same as 1, but fewer than 10 stations pass the filter. All qualifying stations are returned, without padding to 10 rows.
queries:
SELECT observstation
FROM telescopes
GROUP BY observstation
HAVING AVG(bandusagepct) > (SELECT AVG(bandusagepct) FROM telescopes WHERE bandusagepct IS NOT NULL)
SELECT t.observstation, AVG(s.snrratio) AS avg_snr
FROM signals s
JOIN telescopes t ON s.telescref = t.telescregistry
GROUP BY t.observstation
HAVING AVG(s.snrratio) >= (SELECT AVG(snrratio) FROM signals);
SELECT t.observstation
FROM telescopes t
JOIN observatories o ON o.observstation = t.observstation
WHERE t.bandusagepct IS NOT NULL
GROUP BY t.observstation
HAVING AVG(t.bandusagepct) > (
  SELECT AVG(t2.bandusagepct)
  FROM telescopes t2
  JOIN observatories o2 ON o2.observstation = t2.observstation
  WHERE t2.bandusagepct IS NOT NULL
);
SELECT observstation, AVG(bandusagepct) AS avg_bandusagepct
FROM telescopes
WHERE bandusagepct IS NOT NULL
GROUP BY observstation;
SELECT AVG(station_avg) FROM (SELECT AVG(bandusagepct) AS station_avg FROM telescopes GROUP BY observstation);
SELECT t.telescregistry
FROM telescopes t
WHERE t.telescregistry IN (SELECT telescref FROM signals)
  AND t.bandusagepct > (
    SELECT AVG(t2.bandusagepct)
    FROM telescopes t2
    WHERE t2.telescregistry IN (SELECT telescref FROM signals)
  );
